clue.text: Stomach bug overwhelms powerless wimp

indicators.note: one word swamps and encloses the other

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy or miff them

indicators.note: P is the abbreviation for power, so the word loses its P

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
P stands for power in physics

explanation.surface: A tummy bug knocks a feeble weakling flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The midriff is the front of the body between chest and waist, a common loose name for the stomach area.

clue.text: China acquires revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: the friend word takes the revolutionary inside it

parts.note: in cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate
Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: China acquires a revolutionary new weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: cockney rhyming slang from London uses 'china plate' for mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used as a tool and as a weapon.

clue.text: Terrible cut bound to get discoloured

indicators.note: cut removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: dire means terrible or dreadful
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A dreadful cut, once bandaged, is sure to become stained.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirtied has been soiled or stained, so discoloured.

clue.text: State of India's occasionally almost scorching

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of the word
almost drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: scorching means very hot

explanation.surface: India's weather is now and then nearly scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Charm of a Conservative caught by error in end

indicators.note: these letters go inside the destiny word

parts.note: fate is one's end or destiny

indicators.note: the error word catches the other letter inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or error

explanation.surface: A politician is caught out by a blunder at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: As first printed the clue lacked this a, a setter slip; the online clue was corrected to read Charm of a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: To fascinate is to captivate or enchant, the verb sense of charm.

clue.text: Notice old boy's always showing resistance to Left

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, followed by the possessive S

indicators.note: the letter for resistance shifts towards the left, the front of the word

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A former pupil seems to have always resisted the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing resistance to Left' moves the R of EVER leftward, giving ERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to see it or take note of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Floating on lake is river bird

indicators.note: the river sits above the lake letter in this down entry

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers, one in Yorkshire
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A water bird is seen floating on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England; there are several, including the Great Ouse flowing into the Wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird-like thrush; the water ouzel is the dipper.

clue.text: Big equipment, small changes to opening

indicators.note: the letter shifts from the end to the opening, the start

parts.note: trappings are accessories or equipment

explanation.surface: Big equipment and small alterations to an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapping person is big and strong, sturdily built.

clue.text: Capital is managed topping advance

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it
to go on is to proceed or advance

explanation.surface: A capital city is managed better than the advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was formerly the capital of Burma (Myanmar).

clue.text: Reportedly first person with spotted blemish

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: the first-person pronoun I followed by saw, meaning spotted

explanation.surface: Someone says that, at first, they spotted a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a British accent, where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly thing that spoils a view, a blot or blemish.

clue.text: Pens combustible articles about gutless reporter

indicators.note: the coals go around the other piece

parts.note: coals are things that burn

indicators.note: gutless takes the insides out of the word, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone writes about flammable items and a spineless journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrals are enclosures for livestock, the same as pens.

clue.text: Surreal gag doesn't stop Labour's leader …

indicators.note: the strangling word does not keep the following letter, so it drops out

parts.note: to gag can mean to choke or strangle

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political gag fails to silence the leader of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surreal is bizarre and dreamlike, so odd or weird.

clue.text: … rejecting form perhaps with ordinary current leader

indicators.note: rejecting turns the whole string back to front

parts.note: a form is a hare's home, an example of an animal's lair
a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a party head throws out a form, along with an ordinary one in power.
explanation.walkthrough: A hare's 'form' is its resting place, hence lair; 'perhaps' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader in a newspaper is its leading article, the piece giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Bowl over trapping hard shot

indicators.note: the first pieces catch the other one inside

parts.note: a pot is a round vessel, like a bowl
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A bowler takes a wicket and a hard shot gets caught in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a snap taken with a camera, a picture.

clue.text: Give pained expression sitting on butt

indicators.note: the exclamation is placed on top of, after, the other piece

parts.note: a butt is the end, as of a cigarette
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps after sitting down heavily on their backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or a quality, as in endowing a college.

clue.text: Stand controlling strike and catching live rising fish

indicators.note: the waiting word holds the strike word inside it

parts.note: to stand is to wait, as in standing in a queue

indicators.note: the waiting word also catches this next piece, set straight after the strike word

parts.note: to hit is to strike

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads the word upward, backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A stand controls strikes and catches live fish as they rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads BE upwards as EB in this down entry; 'controlling' and 'catching' both put pieces inside WAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the small fry of herring and sprat, eaten whole as fish.

clue.text: Fix pipe oddly making U-turn in great machine

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the word for great

parts.note: ace means excellent or great

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters
the word for fix turns round and runs backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: A plumber repairs a pipe in an odd way, in a great reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making U-turn' turns NAIL backwards to LIAN; 'oddly' keeps PP from 'pipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine, typically a domestic one such as a washer.

clue.text: Stop accepting a student's common

indicators.note: the stopping word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to prevent is to stop
L is the learner plate, the usual crossword sign for a student

explanation.surface: Stopping a student being accepted is common.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread or common.

clue.text: Blasphemy when rejected upset good in church

indicators.note: rejected turns the short word back to front

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for Church of England
to rile is to upset or annoy

explanation.surface: Someone is upset when good is rejected inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something sacred, close in sense to blasphemy.

clue.text: Regret seeing ship's stern while capsizing

indicators.note: in a down entry capsizing turns the string upside down, backwards

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the stern is the end of a ship
as can mean while, as in 'as I spoke'

explanation.surface: Regret on seeing the back of a ship as it overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Regret and sadness are both sorrowful feelings, close synonyms.

clue.text: In secrecy, an idea to give poison

indicators.note: In says the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone plans a secret poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a fast-acting deadly poison.

clue.text: Initially golfer is mad missing easy, easy putt

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A golfer goes mad after missing a very short putt.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a gimme is a putt so short that opponents concede it without it being played.

clue.text: Stick-up traps idiot

indicators.note: in a down entry up reads the word upward, backwards

parts.note: gum is glue, used to stick things
gins are snares or traps for game

explanation.surface: A hold-up ensnares a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is a British informal word for a foolish person, often oneself.

clue.text: He, say, last to move pieces in check

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
the chess pieces go inside the check word

parts.note: a let is a hindrance or check, as in 'without let or hindrance'
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A chess player's final move puts pieces in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the chemical symbol for helium; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is a chemical element, so it is one example of the class.

clue.text: Explorer beginning to do search

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rake is to search thoroughly, as in raking through papers

explanation.surface: An explorer starts out by making a search.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who sailed round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seaman circumnavigated the globe, making him a famous explorer.

clue.text: Drink could make phoney bore heard

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: phoney means sham, fake; a bore is a pain, a nuisance

explanation.surface: A drink might turn a fake bore into someone worth hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine, a celebratory drink.

clue.text: Island summit east, not south

indicators.note: not removes the following letter

parts.note: a crest is the top of a hill

explanation.surface: A climber reaches the summit, facing east rather than south.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Square old man's bearing nearly slow

indicators.note: the father word bears, carries, the other piece inside it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: lazy means sluggish or slow

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned father's manner is almost slow.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: Go abroad missing golf in Dubai?

indicators.note: missing removes the letter from the word

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave to live in another country
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone moves to Dubai, but leaves the golf clubs behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Dubai is an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven states of the United Arab Emirates, each ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Quibbling first woman carrying credit card that's rejected

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: rejected turns the card name back to front

parts.note: Visa is a brand of credit card

explanation.surface: Eve gives excuses when her credit card is declined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rejected' turns VISA round to ASIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive talk dodges the point, which is what quibbling does.

clue.text: Some excess heat heats cover

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A warning that too much heat warms everything around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to encase, as a blade goes into its scabbard, so to cover.

clue.text: Idiosyncrasy going round opposite directions for journey

indicators.note: the trait word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic, a personal quirk
N and S are the compass points north and south, opposite each other

explanation.surface: A traveller's odd habit of taking roundabout routes on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage from one place to another, a journey.
